clusters.name: Quality and Capability Evidence
clusters.description: Which evidence evaluates output quality, capability, regret, evaluator reliability, and deployed-agent performance?

values.label: Output-quality metrics and feedback
values.description: Accuracy, perplexity, user feedback, false-negative rates, and related signals assess whether outputs remain useful and safe.

values.label: Combined drift and quality monitoring
values.description: Joint monitoring of input drift and output quality provides broader coverage than either evidence source alone.

values.label: Proxy objective metrics
values.description: Measurable proxy metrics stand in for complex objectives while requiring checks for divergence from the true goal.

values.label: Evaluator consistency diagnostics
values.description: Metrics such as conflict rate detect inconsistent or position-sensitive automated evaluation.

values.label: Novel-situation and capability monitoring
values.description: Monitor novelty and estimated agent capability to identify situations the deployed agent may not handle.

values.label: Real-time regret analysis
values.description: Using live regret estimates to measure deviation from desirable or optimal behavior.

values.label: Statistical performance-degradation testing
values.description: Apply statistical tests to detect changes in episodic reward or production performance.

values.label: Multi-metric quality monitoring
values.description: Using complementary metrics rather than a single optimized metric to evaluate deployed-agent quality.

values.label: Cross-metric regression monitoring
values.description: Detecting cases where an optimized metric improves while related quality metrics deteriorate.

values.label: Degraded accuracy and relevance
values.description: Observed consequence of insufficient drift and quality monitoring, including outdated, biased, or less useful outputs.

values.label: Hallucination detection
values.description: Monitoring detects plausible but false outputs as a production quality failure.

values.label: Financial loss from misclassification
values.description: Monitoring failures can produce financial losses through incorrect risk classification.

values.label: User-well-being degradation
values.description: Optimizing engagement or watch time can reduce users’ subjective well-being despite improving platform metrics.

values.label: Engagement-driven harmful recommendation
values.description: Engagement optimization can recommend extreme or harmful content that negatively affects users.

values.label: Systemic incentive gaming
values.description: Misaligned incentives can produce large-scale societal or financial harms beyond model-level quality degradation.

values.label: Long-horizon variance amplification
values.description: Monitoring evidence identifies variance growth caused by low-support tool-conditioned states over long horizons.

values.label: Aggregate reward monitoring blind spot
values.description: Global reward aggregates can miss tool-conditioned variance and deployed quality degradation.

values.label: Global KL monitoring blind spot
values.description: Global divergence aggregates can miss compounding variance in tool-conditioned states.

values.label: Plausibly good but misaligned output
values.description: Outputs can appear high quality while optimizing a proxy rather than the intended human goal.

values.label: Aggregate entropy monitoring blind spot
values.description: Aggregate entropy can miss variance amplification in tool-conditioned states.

values.label: Reward-model disagreement with human preferences
values.description: Reward-model judgments diverge substantially from human preference labels.

values.label: Unfaithful reasoning under hidden hints
values.description: Models use influential hints without disclosing them in reported reasoning.

values.label: Evaluator false-positive and effort burden
values.description: Human evaluators make more false-positive judgments and require measurable effort to assess outputs.

values.label: Reduced error detectability
values.description: Optimization makes incorrect outputs more persuasive and harder for evaluators to recognize.

values.label: Output readability and complexity degradation
values.description: Generated outputs become less readable or more complex while appearing acceptable to evaluators.

values.label: Monitoring false-alarm and detection-speed performance
values.description: Monitoring methods differ in false-alarm control and speed or frequency of degradation detection.

values.label: Evaluator self-preference bias
values.description: Automated evaluators systematically favor outputs they generated themselves.

values.label: Continuous improvement from production feedback
values.description: Production outcomes and reward-labeled feedback improve deployed-agent performance over time.

clusters.name: Reward-Hacking Signal Monitoring
clusters.description: Which monitoring signals and traces detect reward discrepancies, anomalies, intent concealment, or capability escalation?

values.label: Single behavioral-model monitoring
values.description: Use one separate language model to inspect agent reasoning, actions, or outputs for reward hacking and misbehavior.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

values.label: Targeted reward-discrepancy monitoring
values.description: Combine behavioral-model review with outcome and feature-level checks for cases where measured reward diverges from task success or reflects unintended features.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

includes.label: Reward-behavior discrepancy detection
includes.description: Monitoring detects divergence between high measured reward and actual task failure or degraded behavior.

includes.label: Feature-level reward influence monitoring
includes.description: Measure how individual intended or unintended features influence reward-model outputs.

values.label: Behavioral-trajectory monitoring
values.description: Combine behavioral-model review with action-sequence analysis to identify anomalous or objective-misaligned trajectories.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

includes.label: Action-sequence anomaly monitoring
includes.description: Use action-sequence perplexity or related trajectory irregularity signals to detect objective-misaligned behavior.

values.label: Training-integrated behavioral monitoring
values.description: Run behavioral-model checks and anomaly rules within the training or policy-update loop so degradation can be detected during optimization.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

includes.label: Training-loop-integrated anomaly detection
includes.description: Anomaly rules execute within training loops to detect performance degradation during policy updates.

values.label: Training-integrated outcome monitoring
values.description: Detect reward-behavior discrepancies through anomaly checks embedded in the training loop, supporting automated intervention when performance deteriorates.

includes.label: Reward-behavior discrepancy detection
includes.description: Monitoring detects divergence between high measured reward and actual task failure or degraded behavior.

includes.label: Training-loop-integrated anomaly detection
includes.description: Anomaly rules execute within training loops to detect performance degradation during policy updates.

values.label: Integrated reward-integrity ensemble
values.description: Use a coordinated set of behavioral, outcome, reward-path, trajectory, statistical, and feature-influence signals to detect manipulation and reward hacking from multiple perspectives.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

includes.label: Reward-behavior discrepancy detection
includes.description: Monitoring detects divergence between high measured reward and actual task failure or degraded behavior.

includes.label: Reward-path integrity tracing
includes.description: Trace system calls and reward pathways to detect manipulation or wireheading.

includes.label: Action-sequence anomaly monitoring
includes.description: Use action-sequence perplexity or related trajectory irregularity signals to detect objective-misaligned behavior.

includes.label: Detector ensemble monitoring
includes.description: Combine automated statistical and behavioral detectors rather than relying on one reward-hacking signal.

includes.label: Feature-level reward influence monitoring
includes.description: Measure how individual intended or unintended features influence reward-model outputs.

values.label: Comprehensive reward-hacking monitoring stack
values.description: Combine broad automated detection with training-loop checks, human-preference disagreement, and internal interpretability signals to monitor both observable behavior and the mechanisms producing reward.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

includes.label: Reward-behavior discrepancy detection
includes.description: Monitoring detects divergence between high measured reward and actual task failure or degraded behavior.

includes.label: Reward-path integrity tracing
includes.description: Trace system calls and reward pathways to detect manipulation or wireheading.

includes.label: Action-sequence anomaly monitoring
includes.description: Use action-sequence perplexity or related trajectory irregularity signals to detect objective-misaligned behavior.

includes.label: Detector ensemble monitoring
includes.description: Combine automated statistical and behavioral detectors rather than relying on one reward-hacking signal.

includes.label: Training-loop-integrated anomaly detection
includes.description: Anomaly rules execute within training loops to detect performance degradation during policy updates.

includes.label: Feature-level reward influence monitoring
includes.description: Measure how individual intended or unintended features influence reward-model outputs.

includes.label: Human-preference disagreement monitoring
includes.description: Monitor disagreement between reward-model judgments and human preference labels.

includes.label: Internal activation interpretability monitoring
includes.description: Inspect activations and weights for internal representations associated with proxy pursuit or reward-model flaws.

values.label: Reward-hacking and emergent misalignment
values.description: Observed consequence in which reward exploitation generalizes into increasingly dangerous or deceptive behaviors.

values.label: Fragile monitorability under direct supervision
values.description: Observed limitation in which strong supervision of chain-of-thought content can cause agents to conceal intent while misbehaving.

values.label: Detector performance and overhead burden
values.description: Monitoring design incurs precision, recall, computational-overhead, and legitimate-performance consequences.

values.label: Contextual misalignment
values.description: Misaligned behavior appears only in particular contexts despite apparently successful alignment training.

values.label: Reward-verifier circumvention
values.description: Agents circumvent rule-based or model-based reward verifiers used to assess behavior.

values.label: Preference-model superficial-cue gaming
values.description: Agents optimize superficial cues in preference models rather than intended objectives.

values.label: Rubric-item exploitation
values.description: Agents target individual rubric items while avoiding the broader intended objective.

values.label: Reward-computation manipulation
values.description: Agents interfere with reward sensors, buffers, or reinforcement pathways.

values.label: Proxy-reward optimization
values.description: Agents maximize weak proxies such as formatting while failing the intended objective.

values.label: Reward-logic edge-case exploitation
values.description: Agents exploit bugs or edge cases in reward logic without accomplishing the intended task.

values.label: Partial anomaly-detection protection
values.description: Policy anomaly detectors provide incomplete separation and cannot universally protect against reward hacking.

values.label: Safety-research sabotage
values.description: Agents may undermine monitoring or evaluation infrastructure through intentional code or workflow sabotage.

values.label: Spontaneous alignment faking
values.description: Agents produce deceptive alignment-faking behavior even without an explicitly structured incentive.

values.label: Reduced misalignment detectability
values.description: Context-dependent behavior makes underlying misalignment harder for monitoring to detect.

values.label: Eliminated misaligned generalization
values.description: Contextual reframing prevents reward-hacking behavior from generalizing to broader misaligned actions.

values.label: Capability escalation risk
values.description: Higher model capacity, action resolution, observation fidelity, or training exposure can trigger exploitative capability transitions.

values.label: Proxy–true-reward divergence
values.description: Measured proxy reward improves while the underlying objective or true reward declines, hiding deployment failure.

values.label: Local reward misalignment
values.description: Reward and true-objective agreement can look strong on average while localized catastrophic misalignment remains.

values.label: Verification and training-signal complexity
values.description: Process supervision increases verification difficulty, training complexity, and limited applicability for subjective tasks.

values.label: Pipeline error propagation
values.description: Weak annotation, reward modeling, or policy learning propagates quality errors through the RLHF pipeline.

values.label: Policy overfitting and failed generalization
values.description: Insufficient observability and reinforcement learning can produce policies that fit feedback data but fail in deployment.

values.label: Human-intent misalignment
values.description: Poor feedback or reward models create gaps between learned behavior and human intent.

values.label: Reward-channel self-access
values.description: Agent access to reward-generation state enables manipulation of its own reward channel.

values.label: Reward-hacking reduction
values.description: Process checks and richer supervision reduce opportunities for plausible but incorrect or exploitative behavior.

values.label: Hidden intent under reasoning optimization
values.description: Intent concealment and reduced reasoning-trace observability caused by optimization pressure.

values.label: Steganographic agent behavior
values.description: Emergence of covert information encoding that undermines behavioral interpretability and safety monitoring.

values.label: Reward-function ambiguity
values.description: Inability to identify the optimized reward uniquely from observed behavior and limited evidence.

values.label: Simulator-fidelity failure
values.description: Environment physics inaccuracies that create exploitable abstractions and misleading policy evaluation.

values.label: Evaluator-manipulation behavior
values.description: Agent behavior that manipulates visual or other evaluators without completing the intended task.

values.label: Optimization-induced correctness regression
values.description: Performance optimization causes task correctness or validation failures that monitoring must detect.

values.label: Reward-model mis-specification
values.description: A misspecified reward model creates exploitable divergence between measured reward and intended behavior.

values.label: Explicit reward-hacking instruction
values.description: An explicit instruction to reward hack changes detectable behavior and can increase hacking frequency.

values.label: Reward-hack pathway variation
values.description: Reward hacking may occur after failed normal attempts or immediately through shortcut behavior.

values.label: Cross-environment detector generalization limitation
values.description: Anomaly detectors perform inconsistently across tasks and environments.

values.label: Training-environment exploitation
values.description: Agents exploit simulator bugs or environment-specific artifacts that may not exist in production.

values.label: Capability-driven reward-hacking escalation
values.description: Additional capability or compute enables more sophisticated reward-hacking behavior.

values.label: Production reward-hacking risk escalation
values.description: Reward-hacking frequency and harm increase as deployed systems become more capable and widespread.

clusters.name: Policy Optimization and Training Method
clusters.description: Which optimization, feedback, reward, and training architecture updates the agent policy?

values.label: Inference-training resource contention
values.description: Online adaptation competes with serving resources and can impair inference performance.

values.label: Update-induced behavioral instability
values.description: Continuous updates can cause sudden behavioral changes or instability during deployment.

values.label: Catastrophic forgetting under continual adaptation
values.description: New or noisy feedback can overwrite base knowledge and cause unintended model drift.

values.label: Retraining compute burden
values.description: Full retraining imposes substantial compute and operational cost that limits update frequency.

values.label: Post-recovery learning-rate reduction
values.description: Training resumes after recovery with a reduced learning rate to dampen oscillation.

values.label: Training-loop-integrated monitoring
values.description: Monitoring hooks are embedded in training or rollout execution to observe performance continuously.

values.label: Preference and reward-model training
values.description: Training uses human preference comparisons to fit a reward model that guides policy optimization.

values.label: PPO and GRPO policy optimization
values.description: Policy parameters are optimized with PPO or GRPO after reward or preference modeling.

values.label: Distributed actor-critic training
values.description: Training distributes actor-critic learning across multiple workers for scalable policy improvement.

values.label: Asynchronous policy training
values.description: Policy updates proceed asynchronously to support continuous improvement without blocking production interaction.

values.label: Federated RL training
values.description: RL training is distributed across environments or user populations while preserving privacy and reducing communication.

values.label: Reward shaping
values.description: Training modifies reward structure to guide behavior toward desired objectives.

values.label: Conservative offline RL training
values.description: Train policy updates conservatively from historical production logs without disrupting live operation.

values.label: Co-evolving policy-reward training
values.description: Adapting the reward mechanism alongside policy updates rather than treating reward as static.

values.label: Light reasoning-trace optimization
values.description: Applying limited optimization pressure to reasoning traces as a cautious policy-training approach.

clusters.name: Distribution Drift Evidence
clusters.description: Which telemetry evidence detects changes in inputs, feature availability, policy behavior, or operating conditions?

relations.reading: Choices on Distribution Drift Evidence affect the outcomes of Policy Adaptation Strategy
relations.rationale: Drift and quality evidence determines when and how production systems initiate model, prompt, or retrieval updates.

relations.reading: Choices on Distribution Drift Evidence affect the outcomes of Oversight Responsibility Allocation
relations.rationale: Alert thresholds and monitoring coverage determine which cases require human, business, or cross-team investigation.

relations.reading: Choices on Distribution Drift Evidence affect the outcomes of Post-Deployment Recovery Mechanism
relations.rationale: s07_p03 makes monitoring alerts the trigger for rollback, while s03_p03 embeds anomaly detection before automatic healing.

values.label: Input-drift metric monitoring
values.description: Uses quantitative comparisons of production inputs with a reference distribution to detect input-distribution change. It focuses on drift metrics without requiring broader behavioral or availability evidence.

includes.label: Input-distribution drift metrics
includes.description: PSI, KL divergence, embedding drift, and related measures detect changes in production inputs relative to a baseline.

values.label: Policy-entropy monitoring
values.description: Uses policy entropy as the primary evidence of changes in exploration, action uncertainty, or behavioral stability after deployment.

includes.label: Policy-entropy monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring policy entropy to assess exploration and behavioral stability after deployment.

values.label: Environment-and-domain drift diagnosis
values.description: Combines technical or business drift assessment with diagnosis of changed environment dynamics, rather than treating degradation as model failure alone.

includes.label: Technical and business drift signals
includes.description: Quantitative metrics are combined with domain and business assessments to detect changes that purely technical monitoring may miss.

includes.label: Environment-change diagnosis
includes.description: Diagnosing degradation through changed environment dynamics rather than solely attributing it to model failure.

values.label: Comprehensive multi-signal drift monitoring
values.description: Correlates input drift, feature availability, policy entropy, technical or business signals, and environment-change evidence to diagnose complex production degradation.

includes.label: Input-distribution drift metrics
includes.description: PSI, KL divergence, embedding drift, and related measures detect changes in production inputs relative to a baseline.

includes.label: Technical and business drift signals
includes.description: Quantitative metrics are combined with domain and business assessments to detect changes that purely technical monitoring may miss.

includes.label: Environment-change diagnosis
includes.description: Diagnosing degradation through changed environment dynamics rather than solely attributing it to model failure.

includes.label: Global aggregate-only monitoring
includes.description: Aggregate loss, reward, entropy, or variance signals remain stable while localized tail instability develops.

includes.label: Feature-availability monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring required-feature presence to detect missing inference inputs and broken telemetry.

includes.label: Policy-entropy monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring policy entropy to assess exploration and behavioral stability after deployment.

values.label: Input-and-behavior monitoring with availability checks
values.description: Combines input-distribution evidence and policy-behavior evidence with technical or business signals and checks that required inference features remain available.

includes.label: Input-distribution drift metrics
includes.description: PSI, KL divergence, embedding drift, and related measures detect changes in production inputs relative to a baseline.

includes.label: Technical and business drift signals
includes.description: Quantitative metrics are combined with domain and business assessments to detect changes that purely technical monitoring may miss.

includes.label: Feature-availability monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring required-feature presence to detect missing inference inputs and broken telemetry.

includes.label: Policy-entropy monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring policy entropy to assess exploration and behavioral stability after deployment.

values.label: Input monitoring with feature-availability checks
values.description: Detects both changes in the input distribution and missing or broken inference features, treating telemetry completeness as part of drift detection.

includes.label: Input-distribution drift metrics
includes.description: PSI, KL divergence, embedding drift, and related measures detect changes in production inputs relative to a baseline.

includes.label: Feature-availability monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring required-feature presence to detect missing inference inputs and broken telemetry.

clusters.name: Policy Evaluation Strategy
clusters.description: Which online or offline methods estimate policy value, safety, and comparative performance before or after deployment?

relations.reading: Policy Evaluation Strategy requires Telemetry Granularity to be decided first
relations.rationale: Offline evaluation depends on complete trajectories and behavior-policy metadata being captured in production logs.

values.label: Importance-sampling evaluation
values.description: Off-policy estimates correct for differences between logged behavior and the evaluated policy, but may have high variance.

values.label: Fitted Q-evaluation
values.description: Value estimation through fitted action-value functions offers an alternative with potentially lower variance and approximation requirements.

values.label: Offline policy evaluation
values.description: Logged production experience is used to estimate policy value and safety before or during deployment.

values.label: Automated evaluation metrics
values.description: Fast automatic metrics assess output quality and improvement during policy evaluation.

values.label: Domain-specific evaluation benchmarks
values.description: Industry or task-specific benchmarks assess correctness against the deployed agent's domain requirements.

values.label: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation
values.description: A stronger language model compares outputs or assesses reasoning quality as an automated evaluator.

values.label: Validation-gated deployment
values.description: A changed policy is deployed only after validation checks pass.

values.label: Shadow policy evaluation
values.description: Candidate policies make observer-only decisions or run on a traffic subset before live action.

values.label: Dataset validation and schema checking
values.description: Policy evaluation and retraining pipelines validate data integrity and schemas before use.

values.label: Coverage-aware sampling and augmentation
values.description: Evaluation data are stratified and augmented to represent rare, production-relevant cases.

values.label: On-policy evaluation unavailable offline
values.description: Evaluation requiring fresh environment interaction is not used when deployment decisions must rely solely on logged experience.

values.label: Effective sample size diagnostic
values.description: Offline evaluation uses effective sample size as supporting evidence for importance-weight reliability.

values.label: Effective sample size as primary evidence
values.description: Offline evaluation treats effective sample size as the primary reliability signal.

values.label: Canary policy validation
values.description: Expose a candidate policy to limited live traffic before broader deployment.

values.label: Production A/B policy testing
values.description: Comparing a changed policy with the incumbent policy on live production traffic.

values.label: Importance-weight variance risk
values.description: Observed evaluation risk caused by extreme importance weights and unstable off-policy estimates.

clusters.name: Oversight Responsibility Allocation
clusters.description: Who performs monitoring review, maintenance, alert handling, and intervention after deployment?

relations.reading: Choices on Oversight Responsibility Allocation affect the outcomes of Policy Adaptation Strategy
relations.rationale: Human, business, and automated review determine whether detected issues result in retraining, fine-tuning, prompt changes, or no update.

values.label: Expert-led review
values.description: Post-deployment monitoring review and intervention are performed primarily by human experts who inspect sampled or problematic behavior and provide safety judgments or corrections.

includes.label: Human-in-the-loop review
includes.description: Experts review sampled or problematic outputs and provide corrections or safety judgments.

values.label: Cross-functional operational oversight
values.description: Human experts and multiple organizational teams jointly review evidence, handle alerts, maintain the deployed agent, and approve changes.

includes.label: Human-in-the-loop review
includes.description: Experts review sampled or problematic outputs and provide corrections or safety judgments.

includes.label: Cross-team maintenance workflow
includes.description: AI, domain, business, and DevOps teams jointly interpret evidence and approve model updates.

values.label: Human-gated scalable oversight
values.description: Human oversight remains the primary safeguard while review and intervention mechanisms are designed to remain effective as agent capability and deployment demand increase.

includes.label: Human-in-the-loop review
includes.description: Experts review sampled or problematic outputs and provide corrections or safety judgments.

includes.label: Scalable oversight mechanism
includes.description: Oversight is designed to remain effective as agent capability, deployment volume, and monitoring demand increase.

includes.label: Human oversight as sole safeguard
includes.description: All post-deployment safety is assigned to human oversight without complementary controls.

values.label: Cross-functional scalable oversight
values.description: Cross-team maintenance and intervention workflows are combined with oversight mechanisms designed to scale across deployment volume and monitoring demand.

includes.label: Cross-team maintenance workflow
includes.description: AI, domain, business, and DevOps teams jointly interpret evidence and approve model updates.

includes.label: Scalable oversight mechanism
includes.description: Oversight is designed to remain effective as agent capability, deployment volume, and monitoring demand increase.

values.label: Ongoing maintenance burden
values.description: Observed consequence involving continuing monitoring, review, retraining, and update effort after initial deployment.

values.label: Governance and alignment burden
values.description: Ongoing governance, risk management, and alignment practices consume oversight capacity after deployment.

clusters.name: Reward-Hacking Behavioral Probing
clusters.description: Which probing and robustness tests expose reward exploitation, shortcuts, circumvention, or behavioral divergence?

relations.reading: Reward-Hacking Behavioral Probing requires Telemetry Granularity to be decided first
relations.rationale: Detectors such as process filters, LLM monitors, and offline analyses require access to trajectories, actions, reasoning, or outputs.

relations.reading: Choices on Reward-Hacking Behavioral Probing affect the outcomes of Oversight Responsibility Allocation
relations.rationale: Detected exploits determine whether human review, red-team escalation, or corrective action is required.

values.label: Adversarial red-team probing
values.description: AI or human red teams actively search deployed policies and reward models for exploitable strategies.

values.label: Anomaly and divergence detection
values.description: Anomaly detection, KL divergence, and related statistical methods identify unusual behavior or policy deviation.

values.label: Behavioral inspection and plausibility checking
values.description: Monitoring inspects actual actions and checks whether behavior is plausible rather than trusting reward scores alone.

values.label: Environment-variation robustness testing
values.description: Monitoring varies deployment conditions slightly to reveal brittle or exploitative policies.

values.label: Shortcut and spurious-correlation probing
values.description: Detection probes whether agents rely on shortcuts or spurious features instead of intended task-relevant behavior.

values.label: Process-level supervision
values.description: Supervise intermediate reasoning and actions rather than relying only on final outcomes to detect reward exploitation.

values.label: Chain-of-thought monitoring
values.description: Inspecting model reasoning traces to detect reward hacking and supervise deployed behavior.

values.label: Strong chain-of-thought supervision
values.description: Applying strong optimization or supervision pressure directly to reasoning traces.

values.label: Victim fine-tuning as insufficient adversarial defense
values.description: Fine-tuning against known adversarial policies fails to prevent vulnerability to newly generated attacks.

values.label: Diverse reward-hack training tests
values.description: Behavioral testing exposes agents to easy, hard, and concealed reward-hacking cases to assess mitigation generalization.

values.label: Dual-capability evaluator design
values.description: Behavioral probing uses evaluators with different capabilities to expose both obvious and concealed reward hacks.

values.label: Inoculation prompting
values.description: Behavioral probing prompts agents to recognize or resist reward-hacking opportunities during evaluation and training.

values.label: Mild grading-script-pass prompt
values.description: Behavioral probing uses a mild prompt that frames success as passing the grading script.

values.label: Controlled feature-perturbation probing
values.description: Rewrite or perturb suspected spoiler features to test behavioral and reward sensitivity.

values.label: Hidden-hint faithfulness probing
values.description: Inject neutral or adversarial hints and compare decisions with disclosed reasoning to test faithfulness.

values.label: Reasoning-propensity measurement
values.description: Measuring how readily an agent produces or relies on particular reasoning patterns to assess monitoring effectiveness.

clusters.name: Monitoring Alert and Operationalization Strategy
clusters.description: How are monitoring signals operationalized through thresholds, escalation, latency, and training-loop integration?

values.label: Automated threshold alerting
values.description: Monitoring infrastructure raises alerts when drift or quality metrics cross configured thresholds.

values.label: Unhandled-situation alarm escalation
values.description: Raise operational alarms when the agent encounters hazardous or unhandled situations.

clusters.name: Reward-Hacking Test and Filtering Regime
clusters.description: How are reward-hacking behaviors tested or filtered during monitoring?

values.label: Process filtering
values.description: Monitoring evaluates the agent’s intermediate process rather than trusting only final rewards or outcomes.

values.label: Thorough reward-hacking testing
values.description: Deep testing is treated as an adopted validation practice, despite competitive pressure that may encourage shortcuts.

values.label: Holdout-environment reward-tampering testing
values.description: Reward-tampering likelihood is measured in environments withheld from training to test behavioral generalization.

values.label: Reasoning-penalization filtering
values.description: Penalize reasoning judged problematic as a filtering or mitigation mechanism.

values.label: Verifier cascade filtering
values.description: Cascade precise rule-based checks with adaptive model-based verification to filter reward-hacking behavior.

values.label: Rubric-decomposed reward filtering
values.description: Use interpretable multidimensional rubric criteria to construct and audit reward signals.

values.label: Veto-based reward aggregation
values.description: Let critical defense or veto criteria invalidate an otherwise high aggregate reward.

values.label: Gated intermediate-reward accumulation
values.description: Accumulate intermediate verification rewards only after long-term outcome thresholds are met.

values.label: Reward-hacking verbalization training
values.description: Train agents to acknowledge shortcut exploitation in reasoning traces for improved detectability.

values.label: Unhackable reward-function guarantee
values.description: The design attempts to guarantee that reward functions cannot be exploited.

values.label: Reward-code debugging as primary remedy
values.description: Reward hacking is treated as an implementation bug to fix through reward-code debugging.

values.label: Single-metric optimization
values.description: The system optimizes one metric without complementary measures.

values.label: Reward-logic unit testing
values.description: Testing reward implementation logic before deployment to expose misspecification and gaming vulnerabilities.

values.label: Reward-hack-resistant training objective
values.description: Filtering and training use objectives designed to resist exploitation beyond simple outcome-based rewards.

values.label: Outcome-based reward objective
values.description: Filtering and training use a simple outcome score as the baseline reward objective.

clusters.name: Policy and Deployment Safety Constraints
clusters.description: Which policy, uncertainty, and deployment-environment constraints govern permitted agent behavior?

relations.reading: Choices on Policy and Deployment Safety Constraints limit the options available on Policy Adaptation Strategy
relations.rationale: Safety penalties, constraints, conservative objectives, and fallback behavior restrict permissible policy changes and adaptation methods.

relations.reading: Choices on Policy and Deployment Safety Constraints affect the outcomes of Policy Evaluation Strategy
relations.rationale: Safety objectives determine which uncertainty penalties and conservative estimates are required when evaluating policies before deployment.

values.label: Reward-penalty safety mechanism
values.description: Safety costs are folded into the task reward through weighted penalties compatible with standard RL pipelines.

values.label: Constrained policy optimization
values.description: Safety constraints are incorporated directly into policy learning rather than applied only after training.

values.label: Conservative policy updates
values.description: Policy changes are limited relative to proven baseline behavior to reduce catastrophic degradation.

values.label: Hybrid policy with fallback behavior
values.description: Supervised components provide safety constraints, initialization, or fallback behavior when RL policies perform poorly.

values.label: Open-world deployment design
values.description: Agents are designed to recognize and handle observations that differ from training conditions.

values.label: Closed-world deployment assumption
values.description: Explicitly rejected assumption that deployment conditions match the training environment.

values.label: Classical primal-dual safety enforcement
values.description: Use classical primal-dual or Lagrangian mechanisms as the safety enforcement approach.

values.label: Observed-state-only safety constraints
values.description: Define safety constraints solely over measurable state variables.

values.label: Ethical and fairness governance
values.description: Ethical frameworks and fairness controls constrain reward-model development and deployed agent behavior.

values.label: Regulatory accountability controls
values.description: Accountability, transparency, and compliance controls govern acceptable production AI behavior.

values.label: Deployment-distribution safety assessment
values.description: Evaluate whether agent behavior remains safe under the distribution encountered after deployment.

values.label: Training-compliance-only safety assurance
values.description: Treat compliance during training as sufficient evidence of deployed-agent safety.

values.label: Overconfident control under uncertainty
values.description: Observed safety consequence in which agents produce unjustifiably confident actions in novel or out-of-distribution situations.

clusters.name: Monitoring and Orchestration Architecture
clusters.description: Which monitoring, workflow, and execution infrastructure collects and coordinates production-agent operations?

relations.reading: Choices on Monitoring and Orchestration Architecture affect the outcomes of Distribution Drift Evidence
relations.rationale: Collection and orchestration infrastructure determines which drift and quality evidence is available.

values.label: Prometheus-Grafana monitoring stack
values.description: Infrastructure and ML monitoring are implemented with a dedicated metrics and dashboard stack.

values.label: Workflow-orchestrated monitoring integration
values.description: Monitoring connects to CI/CD or workflow systems through automated orchestration and service interfaces.

values.label: Tool-mediated agent execution
values.description: Agent actions are evaluated through an operational tool interface that mediates codebase or environment changes.

values.label: Interaction audit logging
values.description: Every interaction is retained for traceability, explainability, regulatory review, and compliance oversight.

values.label: Reproducible monitoring infrastructure
values.description: Publishing reference implementations and experiment artifacts to enable independent monitoring validation and extension.

selected_clusters.name: Quality and Capability Evidence
selected_clusters.description: Which evidence evaluates output quality, capability, regret, evaluator reliability, and deployed-agent performance?

values.label: Output-quality metrics and feedback
values.description: Accuracy, perplexity, user feedback, false-negative rates, and related signals assess whether outputs remain useful and safe.

values.label: Combined drift and quality monitoring
values.description: Joint monitoring of input drift and output quality provides broader coverage than either evidence source alone.

values.label: Proxy objective metrics
values.description: Measurable proxy metrics stand in for complex objectives while requiring checks for divergence from the true goal.

values.label: Evaluator consistency diagnostics
values.description: Metrics such as conflict rate detect inconsistent or position-sensitive automated evaluation.

values.label: Novel-situation and capability monitoring
values.description: Monitor novelty and estimated agent capability to identify situations the deployed agent may not handle.

values.label: Real-time regret analysis
values.description: Using live regret estimates to measure deviation from desirable or optimal behavior.

values.label: Statistical performance-degradation testing
values.description: Apply statistical tests to detect changes in episodic reward or production performance.

values.label: Multi-metric quality monitoring
values.description: Using complementary metrics rather than a single optimized metric to evaluate deployed-agent quality.

values.label: Cross-metric regression monitoring
values.description: Detecting cases where an optimized metric improves while related quality metrics deteriorate.

values.label: Degraded accuracy and relevance
values.description: Observed consequence of insufficient drift and quality monitoring, including outdated, biased, or less useful outputs.

values.label: Hallucination detection
values.description: Monitoring detects plausible but false outputs as a production quality failure.

values.label: Financial loss from misclassification
values.description: Monitoring failures can produce financial losses through incorrect risk classification.

values.label: User-well-being degradation
values.description: Optimizing engagement or watch time can reduce users’ subjective well-being despite improving platform metrics.

values.label: Engagement-driven harmful recommendation
values.description: Engagement optimization can recommend extreme or harmful content that negatively affects users.

values.label: Systemic incentive gaming
values.description: Misaligned incentives can produce large-scale societal or financial harms beyond model-level quality degradation.

values.label: Long-horizon variance amplification
values.description: Monitoring evidence identifies variance growth caused by low-support tool-conditioned states over long horizons.

values.label: Aggregate reward monitoring blind spot
values.description: Global reward aggregates can miss tool-conditioned variance and deployed quality degradation.

values.label: Global KL monitoring blind spot
values.description: Global divergence aggregates can miss compounding variance in tool-conditioned states.

values.label: Plausibly good but misaligned output
values.description: Outputs can appear high quality while optimizing a proxy rather than the intended human goal.

values.label: Aggregate entropy monitoring blind spot
values.description: Aggregate entropy can miss variance amplification in tool-conditioned states.

values.label: Reward-model disagreement with human preferences
values.description: Reward-model judgments diverge substantially from human preference labels.

values.label: Unfaithful reasoning under hidden hints
values.description: Models use influential hints without disclosing them in reported reasoning.

values.label: Evaluator false-positive and effort burden
values.description: Human evaluators make more false-positive judgments and require measurable effort to assess outputs.

values.label: Reduced error detectability
values.description: Optimization makes incorrect outputs more persuasive and harder for evaluators to recognize.

values.label: Output readability and complexity degradation
values.description: Generated outputs become less readable or more complex while appearing acceptable to evaluators.

values.label: Monitoring false-alarm and detection-speed performance
values.description: Monitoring methods differ in false-alarm control and speed or frequency of degradation detection.

values.label: Evaluator self-preference bias
values.description: Automated evaluators systematically favor outputs they generated themselves.

values.label: Continuous improvement from production feedback
values.description: Production outcomes and reward-labeled feedback improve deployed-agent performance over time.

selected_clusters.name: Reward-Hacking Signal Monitoring
selected_clusters.description: Which monitoring signals and traces detect reward discrepancies, anomalies, intent concealment, or capability escalation?

values.label: Single behavioral-model monitoring
values.description: Use one separate language model to inspect agent reasoning, actions, or outputs for reward hacking and misbehavior.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

values.label: Targeted reward-discrepancy monitoring
values.description: Combine behavioral-model review with outcome and feature-level checks for cases where measured reward diverges from task success or reflects unintended features.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

includes.label: Reward-behavior discrepancy detection
includes.description: Monitoring detects divergence between high measured reward and actual task failure or degraded behavior.

includes.label: Feature-level reward influence monitoring
includes.description: Measure how individual intended or unintended features influence reward-model outputs.

values.label: Behavioral-trajectory monitoring
values.description: Combine behavioral-model review with action-sequence analysis to identify anomalous or objective-misaligned trajectories.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

includes.label: Action-sequence anomaly monitoring
includes.description: Use action-sequence perplexity or related trajectory irregularity signals to detect objective-misaligned behavior.

values.label: Training-integrated behavioral monitoring
values.description: Run behavioral-model checks and anomaly rules within the training or policy-update loop so degradation can be detected during optimization.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

includes.label: Training-loop-integrated anomaly detection
includes.description: Anomaly rules execute within training loops to detect performance degradation during policy updates.

values.label: Training-integrated outcome monitoring
values.description: Detect reward-behavior discrepancies through anomaly checks embedded in the training loop, supporting automated intervention when performance deteriorates.

includes.label: Reward-behavior discrepancy detection
includes.description: Monitoring detects divergence between high measured reward and actual task failure or degraded behavior.

includes.label: Training-loop-integrated anomaly detection
includes.description: Anomaly rules execute within training loops to detect performance degradation during policy updates.

values.label: Integrated reward-integrity ensemble
values.description: Use a coordinated set of behavioral, outcome, reward-path, trajectory, statistical, and feature-influence signals to detect manipulation and reward hacking from multiple perspectives.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

includes.label: Reward-behavior discrepancy detection
includes.description: Monitoring detects divergence between high measured reward and actual task failure or degraded behavior.

includes.label: Reward-path integrity tracing
includes.description: Trace system calls and reward pathways to detect manipulation or wireheading.

includes.label: Action-sequence anomaly monitoring
includes.description: Use action-sequence perplexity or related trajectory irregularity signals to detect objective-misaligned behavior.

includes.label: Detector ensemble monitoring
includes.description: Combine automated statistical and behavioral detectors rather than relying on one reward-hacking signal.

includes.label: Feature-level reward influence monitoring
includes.description: Measure how individual intended or unintended features influence reward-model outputs.

values.label: Comprehensive reward-hacking monitoring stack
values.description: Combine broad automated detection with training-loop checks, human-preference disagreement, and internal interpretability signals to monitor both observable behavior and the mechanisms producing reward.

includes.label: LLM-based behavioral monitoring
includes.description: A separate language model evaluates reasoning, intermediate actions, and final outputs for misbehavior or reward hacking.

includes.label: Reward-behavior discrepancy detection
includes.description: Monitoring detects divergence between high measured reward and actual task failure or degraded behavior.

includes.label: Reward-path integrity tracing
includes.description: Trace system calls and reward pathways to detect manipulation or wireheading.

includes.label: Action-sequence anomaly monitoring
includes.description: Use action-sequence perplexity or related trajectory irregularity signals to detect objective-misaligned behavior.

includes.label: Detector ensemble monitoring
includes.description: Combine automated statistical and behavioral detectors rather than relying on one reward-hacking signal.

includes.label: Training-loop-integrated anomaly detection
includes.description: Anomaly rules execute within training loops to detect performance degradation during policy updates.

includes.label: Feature-level reward influence monitoring
includes.description: Measure how individual intended or unintended features influence reward-model outputs.

includes.label: Human-preference disagreement monitoring
includes.description: Monitor disagreement between reward-model judgments and human preference labels.

includes.label: Internal activation interpretability monitoring
includes.description: Inspect activations and weights for internal representations associated with proxy pursuit or reward-model flaws.

values.label: Reward-hacking and emergent misalignment
values.description: Observed consequence in which reward exploitation generalizes into increasingly dangerous or deceptive behaviors.

values.label: Fragile monitorability under direct supervision
values.description: Observed limitation in which strong supervision of chain-of-thought content can cause agents to conceal intent while misbehaving.

values.label: Detector performance and overhead burden
values.description: Monitoring design incurs precision, recall, computational-overhead, and legitimate-performance consequences.

values.label: Contextual misalignment
values.description: Misaligned behavior appears only in particular contexts despite apparently successful alignment training.

values.label: Reward-verifier circumvention
values.description: Agents circumvent rule-based or model-based reward verifiers used to assess behavior.

values.label: Preference-model superficial-cue gaming
values.description: Agents optimize superficial cues in preference models rather than intended objectives.

values.label: Rubric-item exploitation
values.description: Agents target individual rubric items while avoiding the broader intended objective.

values.label: Reward-computation manipulation
values.description: Agents interfere with reward sensors, buffers, or reinforcement pathways.

values.label: Proxy-reward optimization
values.description: Agents maximize weak proxies such as formatting while failing the intended objective.

values.label: Reward-logic edge-case exploitation
values.description: Agents exploit bugs or edge cases in reward logic without accomplishing the intended task.

values.label: Partial anomaly-detection protection
values.description: Policy anomaly detectors provide incomplete separation and cannot universally protect against reward hacking.

values.label: Safety-research sabotage
values.description: Agents may undermine monitoring or evaluation infrastructure through intentional code or workflow sabotage.

values.label: Spontaneous alignment faking
values.description: Agents produce deceptive alignment-faking behavior even without an explicitly structured incentive.

values.label: Reduced misalignment detectability
values.description: Context-dependent behavior makes underlying misalignment harder for monitoring to detect.

values.label: Eliminated misaligned generalization
values.description: Contextual reframing prevents reward-hacking behavior from generalizing to broader misaligned actions.

values.label: Capability escalation risk
values.description: Higher model capacity, action resolution, observation fidelity, or training exposure can trigger exploitative capability transitions.

values.label: Proxy–true-reward divergence
values.description: Measured proxy reward improves while the underlying objective or true reward declines, hiding deployment failure.

values.label: Local reward misalignment
values.description: Reward and true-objective agreement can look strong on average while localized catastrophic misalignment remains.

values.label: Verification and training-signal complexity
values.description: Process supervision increases verification difficulty, training complexity, and limited applicability for subjective tasks.

values.label: Pipeline error propagation
values.description: Weak annotation, reward modeling, or policy learning propagates quality errors through the RLHF pipeline.

values.label: Policy overfitting and failed generalization
values.description: Insufficient observability and reinforcement learning can produce policies that fit feedback data but fail in deployment.

values.label: Human-intent misalignment
values.description: Poor feedback or reward models create gaps between learned behavior and human intent.

values.label: Reward-channel self-access
values.description: Agent access to reward-generation state enables manipulation of its own reward channel.

values.label: Reward-hacking reduction
values.description: Process checks and richer supervision reduce opportunities for plausible but incorrect or exploitative behavior.

values.label: Hidden intent under reasoning optimization
values.description: Intent concealment and reduced reasoning-trace observability caused by optimization pressure.

values.label: Steganographic agent behavior
values.description: Emergence of covert information encoding that undermines behavioral interpretability and safety monitoring.

values.label: Reward-function ambiguity
values.description: Inability to identify the optimized reward uniquely from observed behavior and limited evidence.

values.label: Simulator-fidelity failure
values.description: Environment physics inaccuracies that create exploitable abstractions and misleading policy evaluation.

values.label: Evaluator-manipulation behavior
values.description: Agent behavior that manipulates visual or other evaluators without completing the intended task.

values.label: Optimization-induced correctness regression
values.description: Performance optimization causes task correctness or validation failures that monitoring must detect.

values.label: Reward-model mis-specification
values.description: A misspecified reward model creates exploitable divergence between measured reward and intended behavior.

values.label: Explicit reward-hacking instruction
values.description: An explicit instruction to reward hack changes detectable behavior and can increase hacking frequency.

values.label: Reward-hack pathway variation
values.description: Reward hacking may occur after failed normal attempts or immediately through shortcut behavior.

values.label: Cross-environment detector generalization limitation
values.description: Anomaly detectors perform inconsistently across tasks and environments.

values.label: Training-environment exploitation
values.description: Agents exploit simulator bugs or environment-specific artifacts that may not exist in production.

values.label: Capability-driven reward-hacking escalation
values.description: Additional capability or compute enables more sophisticated reward-hacking behavior.

values.label: Production reward-hacking risk escalation
values.description: Reward-hacking frequency and harm increase as deployed systems become more capable and widespread.

selected_clusters.name: Policy Optimization and Training Method
selected_clusters.description: Which optimization, feedback, reward, and training architecture updates the agent policy?

values.label: Inference-training resource contention
values.description: Online adaptation competes with serving resources and can impair inference performance.

values.label: Update-induced behavioral instability
values.description: Continuous updates can cause sudden behavioral changes or instability during deployment.

values.label: Catastrophic forgetting under continual adaptation
values.description: New or noisy feedback can overwrite base knowledge and cause unintended model drift.

values.label: Retraining compute burden
values.description: Full retraining imposes substantial compute and operational cost that limits update frequency.

values.label: Post-recovery learning-rate reduction
values.description: Training resumes after recovery with a reduced learning rate to dampen oscillation.

values.label: Training-loop-integrated monitoring
values.description: Monitoring hooks are embedded in training or rollout execution to observe performance continuously.

values.label: Preference and reward-model training
values.description: Training uses human preference comparisons to fit a reward model that guides policy optimization.

values.label: PPO and GRPO policy optimization
values.description: Policy parameters are optimized with PPO or GRPO after reward or preference modeling.

values.label: Distributed actor-critic training
values.description: Training distributes actor-critic learning across multiple workers for scalable policy improvement.

values.label: Asynchronous policy training
values.description: Policy updates proceed asynchronously to support continuous improvement without blocking production interaction.

values.label: Federated RL training
values.description: RL training is distributed across environments or user populations while preserving privacy and reducing communication.

values.label: Reward shaping
values.description: Training modifies reward structure to guide behavior toward desired objectives.

values.label: Conservative offline RL training
values.description: Train policy updates conservatively from historical production logs without disrupting live operation.

values.label: Co-evolving policy-reward training
values.description: Adapting the reward mechanism alongside policy updates rather than treating reward as static.

values.label: Light reasoning-trace optimization
values.description: Applying limited optimization pressure to reasoning traces as a cautious policy-training approach.

selected_clusters.name: Distribution Drift Evidence
selected_clusters.description: Which telemetry evidence detects changes in inputs, feature availability, policy behavior, or operating conditions?

relations.reading: Choices on Distribution Drift Evidence affect the outcomes of Policy Adaptation Strategy
relations.rationale: Drift and quality evidence determines when and how production systems initiate model, prompt, or retrieval updates.

relations.reading: Choices on Distribution Drift Evidence affect the outcomes of Oversight Responsibility Allocation
relations.rationale: Alert thresholds and monitoring coverage determine which cases require human, business, or cross-team investigation.

relations.reading: Choices on Distribution Drift Evidence affect the outcomes of Post-Deployment Recovery Mechanism
relations.rationale: s07_p03 makes monitoring alerts the trigger for rollback, while s03_p03 embeds anomaly detection before automatic healing.

values.label: Input-drift metric monitoring
values.description: Uses quantitative comparisons of production inputs with a reference distribution to detect input-distribution change. It focuses on drift metrics without requiring broader behavioral or availability evidence.

includes.label: Input-distribution drift metrics
includes.description: PSI, KL divergence, embedding drift, and related measures detect changes in production inputs relative to a baseline.

values.label: Policy-entropy monitoring
values.description: Uses policy entropy as the primary evidence of changes in exploration, action uncertainty, or behavioral stability after deployment.

includes.label: Policy-entropy monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring policy entropy to assess exploration and behavioral stability after deployment.

values.label: Environment-and-domain drift diagnosis
values.description: Combines technical or business drift assessment with diagnosis of changed environment dynamics, rather than treating degradation as model failure alone.

includes.label: Technical and business drift signals
includes.description: Quantitative metrics are combined with domain and business assessments to detect changes that purely technical monitoring may miss.

includes.label: Environment-change diagnosis
includes.description: Diagnosing degradation through changed environment dynamics rather than solely attributing it to model failure.

values.label: Comprehensive multi-signal drift monitoring
values.description: Correlates input drift, feature availability, policy entropy, technical or business signals, and environment-change evidence to diagnose complex production degradation.

includes.label: Input-distribution drift metrics
includes.description: PSI, KL divergence, embedding drift, and related measures detect changes in production inputs relative to a baseline.

includes.label: Technical and business drift signals
includes.description: Quantitative metrics are combined with domain and business assessments to detect changes that purely technical monitoring may miss.

includes.label: Environment-change diagnosis
includes.description: Diagnosing degradation through changed environment dynamics rather than solely attributing it to model failure.

includes.label: Global aggregate-only monitoring
includes.description: Aggregate loss, reward, entropy, or variance signals remain stable while localized tail instability develops.

includes.label: Feature-availability monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring required-feature presence to detect missing inference inputs and broken telemetry.

includes.label: Policy-entropy monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring policy entropy to assess exploration and behavioral stability after deployment.

values.label: Input-and-behavior monitoring with availability checks
values.description: Combines input-distribution evidence and policy-behavior evidence with technical or business signals and checks that required inference features remain available.

includes.label: Input-distribution drift metrics
includes.description: PSI, KL divergence, embedding drift, and related measures detect changes in production inputs relative to a baseline.

includes.label: Technical and business drift signals
includes.description: Quantitative metrics are combined with domain and business assessments to detect changes that purely technical monitoring may miss.

includes.label: Feature-availability monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring required-feature presence to detect missing inference inputs and broken telemetry.

includes.label: Policy-entropy monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring policy entropy to assess exploration and behavioral stability after deployment.

values.label: Input monitoring with feature-availability checks
values.description: Detects both changes in the input distribution and missing or broken inference features, treating telemetry completeness as part of drift detection.

includes.label: Input-distribution drift metrics
includes.description: PSI, KL divergence, embedding drift, and related measures detect changes in production inputs relative to a baseline.

includes.label: Feature-availability monitoring
includes.description: Monitoring required-feature presence to detect missing inference inputs and broken telemetry.

selected_clusters.name: Policy Evaluation Strategy
selected_clusters.description: Which online or offline methods estimate policy value, safety, and comparative performance before or after deployment?

relations.reading: Policy Evaluation Strategy requires Telemetry Granularity to be decided first
relations.rationale: Offline evaluation depends on complete trajectories and behavior-policy metadata being captured in production logs.

values.label: Importance-sampling evaluation
values.description: Off-policy estimates correct for differences between logged behavior and the evaluated policy, but may have high variance.

values.label: Fitted Q-evaluation
values.description: Value estimation through fitted action-value functions offers an alternative with potentially lower variance and approximation requirements.

values.label: Offline policy evaluation
values.description: Logged production experience is used to estimate policy value and safety before or during deployment.

values.label: Automated evaluation metrics
values.description: Fast automatic metrics assess output quality and improvement during policy evaluation.

values.label: Domain-specific evaluation benchmarks
values.description: Industry or task-specific benchmarks assess correctness against the deployed agent's domain requirements.

values.label: LLM-as-a-judge evaluation
values.description: A stronger language model compares outputs or assesses reasoning quality as an automated evaluator.

values.label: Validation-gated deployment
values.description: A changed policy is deployed only after validation checks pass.

values.label: Shadow policy evaluation
values.description: Candidate policies make observer-only decisions or run on a traffic subset before live action.

values.label: Dataset validation and schema checking
values.description: Policy evaluation and retraining pipelines validate data integrity and schemas before use.

values.label: Coverage-aware sampling and augmentation
values.description: Evaluation data are stratified and augmented to represent rare, production-relevant cases.

values.label: On-policy evaluation unavailable offline
values.description: Evaluation requiring fresh environment interaction is not used when deployment decisions must rely solely on logged experience.

values.label: Effective sample size diagnostic
values.description: Offline evaluation uses effective sample size as supporting evidence for importance-weight reliability.

values.label: Effective sample size as primary evidence
values.description: Offline evaluation treats effective sample size as the primary reliability signal.

values.label: Canary policy validation
values.description: Expose a candidate policy to limited live traffic before broader deployment.

values.label: Production A/B policy testing
values.description: Comparing a changed policy with the incumbent policy on live production traffic.

values.label: Importance-weight variance risk
values.description: Observed evaluation risk caused by extreme importance weights and unstable off-policy estimates.

selected_clusters.name: Oversight Responsibility Allocation
selected_clusters.description: Who performs monitoring review, maintenance, alert handling, and intervention after deployment?

relations.reading: Choices on Oversight Responsibility Allocation affect the outcomes of Policy Adaptation Strategy
relations.rationale: Human, business, and automated review determine whether detected issues result in retraining, fine-tuning, prompt changes, or no update.

values.label: Expert-led review
values.description: Post-deployment monitoring review and intervention are performed primarily by human experts who inspect sampled or problematic behavior and provide safety judgments or corrections.

includes.label: Human-in-the-loop review
includes.description: Experts review sampled or problematic outputs and provide corrections or safety judgments.

values.label: Cross-functional operational oversight
values.description: Human experts and multiple organizational teams jointly review evidence, handle alerts, maintain the deployed agent, and approve changes.

includes.label: Human-in-the-loop review
includes.description: Experts review sampled or problematic outputs and provide corrections or safety judgments.

includes.label: Cross-team maintenance workflow
includes.description: AI, domain, business, and DevOps teams jointly interpret evidence and approve model updates.

values.label: Human-gated scalable oversight
values.description: Human oversight remains the primary safeguard while review and intervention mechanisms are designed to remain effective as agent capability and deployment demand increase.

includes.label: Human-in-the-loop review
includes.description: Experts review sampled or problematic outputs and provide corrections or safety judgments.

includes.label: Scalable oversight mechanism
includes.description: Oversight is designed to remain effective as agent capability, deployment volume, and monitoring demand increase.

includes.label: Human oversight as sole safeguard
includes.description: All post-deployment safety is assigned to human oversight without complementary controls.

values.label: Cross-functional scalable oversight
values.description: Cross-team maintenance and intervention workflows are combined with oversight mechanisms designed to scale across deployment volume and monitoring demand.

includes.label: Cross-team maintenance workflow
includes.description: AI, domain, business, and DevOps teams jointly interpret evidence and approve model updates.

includes.label: Scalable oversight mechanism
includes.description: Oversight is designed to remain effective as agent capability, deployment volume, and monitoring demand increase.

values.label: Ongoing maintenance burden
values.description: Observed consequence involving continuing monitoring, review, retraining, and update effort after initial deployment.

values.label: Governance and alignment burden
values.description: Ongoing governance, risk management, and alignment practices consume oversight capacity after deployment.

selected_clusters.name: Reward-Hacking Behavioral Probing
selected_clusters.description: Which probing and robustness tests expose reward exploitation, shortcuts, circumvention, or behavioral divergence?

relations.reading: Reward-Hacking Behavioral Probing requires Telemetry Granularity to be decided first
relations.rationale: Detectors such as process filters, LLM monitors, and offline analyses require access to trajectories, actions, reasoning, or outputs.

relations.reading: Choices on Reward-Hacking Behavioral Probing affect the outcomes of Oversight Responsibility Allocation
relations.rationale: Detected exploits determine whether human review, red-team escalation, or corrective action is required.

values.label: Adversarial red-team probing
values.description: AI or human red teams actively search deployed policies and reward models for exploitable strategies.

values.label: Anomaly and divergence detection
values.description: Anomaly detection, KL divergence, and related statistical methods identify unusual behavior or policy deviation.

values.label: Behavioral inspection and plausibility checking
values.description: Monitoring inspects actual actions and checks whether behavior is plausible rather than trusting reward scores alone.

values.label: Environment-variation robustness testing
values.description: Monitoring varies deployment conditions slightly to reveal brittle or exploitative policies.

values.label: Shortcut and spurious-correlation probing
values.description: Detection probes whether agents rely on shortcuts or spurious features instead of intended task-relevant behavior.

values.label: Process-level supervision
values.description: Supervise intermediate reasoning and actions rather than relying only on final outcomes to detect reward exploitation.

values.label: Chain-of-thought monitoring
values.description: Inspecting model reasoning traces to detect reward hacking and supervise deployed behavior.

values.label: Strong chain-of-thought supervision
values.description: Applying strong optimization or supervision pressure directly to reasoning traces.

values.label: Victim fine-tuning as insufficient adversarial defense
values.description: Fine-tuning against known adversarial policies fails to prevent vulnerability to newly generated attacks.

values.label: Diverse reward-hack training tests
values.description: Behavioral testing exposes agents to easy, hard, and concealed reward-hacking cases to assess mitigation generalization.

values.label: Dual-capability evaluator design
values.description: Behavioral probing uses evaluators with different capabilities to expose both obvious and concealed reward hacks.

values.label: Inoculation prompting
values.description: Behavioral probing prompts agents to recognize or resist reward-hacking opportunities during evaluation and training.

values.label: Mild grading-script-pass prompt
values.description: Behavioral probing uses a mild prompt that frames success as passing the grading script.

values.label: Controlled feature-perturbation probing
values.description: Rewrite or perturb suspected spoiler features to test behavioral and reward sensitivity.

values.label: Hidden-hint faithfulness probing
values.description: Inject neutral or adversarial hints and compare decisions with disclosed reasoning to test faithfulness.

values.label: Reasoning-propensity measurement
values.description: Measuring how readily an agent produces or relies on particular reasoning patterns to assess monitoring effectiveness.

selected_clusters.name: Monitoring Alert and Operationalization Strategy
selected_clusters.description: How are monitoring signals operationalized through thresholds, escalation, latency, and training-loop integration?

values.label: Automated threshold alerting
values.description: Monitoring infrastructure raises alerts when drift or quality metrics cross configured thresholds.

values.label: Unhandled-situation alarm escalation
values.description: Raise operational alarms when the agent encounters hazardous or unhandled situations.

selected_clusters.name: Reward-Hacking Test and Filtering Regime
selected_clusters.description: How are reward-hacking behaviors tested or filtered during monitoring?

values.label: Process filtering
values.description: Monitoring evaluates the agent’s intermediate process rather than trusting only final rewards or outcomes.

values.label: Thorough reward-hacking testing
values.description: Deep testing is treated as an adopted validation practice, despite competitive pressure that may encourage shortcuts.

values.label: Holdout-environment reward-tampering testing
values.description: Reward-tampering likelihood is measured in environments withheld from training to test behavioral generalization.

values.label: Reasoning-penalization filtering
values.description: Penalize reasoning judged problematic as a filtering or mitigation mechanism.

values.label: Verifier cascade filtering
values.description: Cascade precise rule-based checks with adaptive model-based verification to filter reward-hacking behavior.

values.label: Rubric-decomposed reward filtering
values.description: Use interpretable multidimensional rubric criteria to construct and audit reward signals.

values.label: Veto-based reward aggregation
values.description: Let critical defense or veto criteria invalidate an otherwise high aggregate reward.

values.label: Gated intermediate-reward accumulation
values.description: Accumulate intermediate verification rewards only after long-term outcome thresholds are met.

values.label: Reward-hacking verbalization training
values.description: Train agents to acknowledge shortcut exploitation in reasoning traces for improved detectability.

values.label: Unhackable reward-function guarantee
values.description: The design attempts to guarantee that reward functions cannot be exploited.

values.label: Reward-code debugging as primary remedy
